opening_message: My headphones from order ORD-7113 are broken AGAIN. This is the fourth time! I have a warranty — can you fix them?

task_rules: Keep the request scoped to resolving the defective headphones from ORD-7113 through the best practical no-cost option, starting from the warranty issue but not insisting on another warranty repair if a better valid path exists.

Provide the order ID, item, and recurring defect details when asked, but do not volunteer policy rules, refund amounts, delivery timing, warranty claim counts, or return eligibility as user-known facts.

If the agent says the warranty is maxed out, offers a paid repair, or focuses only on warranty handling, ask the agent to check whether the recently delivered defective headphones can instead be returned or refunded at no cost.

Push back if the agent denies or skips the return option without checking return eligibility, proposes a paid repair, replacement, partial workaround, or warranty-only path, or treats the defect as a changed-mind return.
Accept only a defective-return path that is presented as better than the paid repair and includes a full refund to the original payment method, no restocking fee, and a return label.
If the agent asks for confirmation before showing the return preview details, ask for the refund amount, reason, fees, label, and refund method before agreeing.
End only after the agent confirms the defective return has been processed for the headphones with the full $249 refund, no restocking fee, original-payment refund method, and return label issued.
user_simulator.user_sim_context: Your headphones have broken again after repeated warranty issues, and you are exhausted with the cycle of fixes. What you want most is the best practical outcome now, not another abstract explanation of coverage. You expect the agent to look at the full situation and tell you the smartest path available today.

task_summary:
**Task:** The customer has defective headphones with a maxed-out warranty claim history, but the item was delivered only ten days ago and is still fully returnable. The correct handling is to recognize that the open return window provides a better valid resolution than the paid repair path and to process the full refund route.

**Challenge:** The trap is stopping at the first policy dead end. Weak agents see the warranty cap, offer the $99 repair, and never look for the still-available return option that actually resolves the case better.

task_requirements.requirement: Agent must explain that the warranty is maxed out and that a defective return is the better available option because it provides a full $249 refund instead of a paid repair.
Agent must call get_policies with topic return after checking the maxed warranty and before processing the final return.
